# Servo positioning -- TIA Portal starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The function block's body is yours.*

**The task.** Shuttle the axis between station A at 100 mm and station B, the panel's pot, dwelling a second at each, from Start until Stop. The drive does nothing until axis.enable has been on long enough for axis.ready, and every move needs axis.velocity as well as axis.target. When the drive faults it stops itself and latches axis.error: hold your sequence, show it, and acknowledge -- a rising edge of axis.ack -- only when the operator presses Reset and axis.fault has gone.

**Done when.** The carriage stops on A and on B in turn, and on the new B as soon as you turn the pot. Raise axis.fault mid-move and the carriage quick-stops; clear it, and nothing moves until somebody presses Reset -- a program that acknowledges on its own is automatic restart by another name. Careful with inposition: on the scan that writes a new target it still describes the old one, so arrive on axis.position against the station you are going to.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`servo_positioning.scl`](servo_positioning.scl) | SCL source: the global DB `FF_IO` with every signal, and an empty FB `"ServoPositioning"`. |
| [`opcua_mapping.json`](opcua_mapping.json) | For `--driver opcua-client`: tag id -> `ns=3;s="FF_IO"."..."`. |
| [`snap7_mapping.json`](snap7_mapping.json) | For `--driver s7-snap7`: tag id -> `DBX`/`DBD` offset in `FF_IO`. |
| [`plcsim_mapping.json`](plcsim_mapping.json) | For `--driver plcsim-advanced`: tag id -> `FF_IO.<Name>`. |

NodeIds -- is [`../README.md`](../README.md). This page is only what is
different about this scene.

## Set it up

1. In a project with an S7-1500 CPU: *External source files -> Add new
   external file*, pick `servo_positioning.scl`, then right-click it -> *Generate
   blocks from source*. That creates `FF_IO` and `"ServoPositioning"`. One
   exercise per CPU: this `FF_IO` replaces any other one.
2. Call `"ServoPositioning"` from OB1 (drag it into `Main`; TIA creates the
   instance DB).
3. Check `FF_IO`'s properties: *Optimized block access* off (the source sets
   it), *Accessible from HMI/OPC UA* and *Writable from HMI/OPC UA* on for
   every member (TIA's default). Without *Writable* every sensor reads FALSE
   forever.
4. Compile, download, RUN.

## Run it

Open the scene in FactoryForge first (pick "Servo positioning" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/servo_positioning.json)), then attach
the sidecar with whichever driver reaches your CPU:

```bash
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver opcua-client --mapping examples/tia/servo-positioning/opcua_mapping.json -o url opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host <cpu-ip> -o db <FF_IO's number> --mapping examples/tia/servo-positioning/snap7_mapping.json
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver plcsim-advanced -o instance <name> --mapping examples/tia/servo-positioning/plcsim_mapping.json
```

(From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar` in place of
`factoryforge-sidecar`, run from the repository root so the paths resolve.)
To have it marked, run `python tools/grade.py --scene servo-positioning` in place
of the 3D scene and add the `--port` it prints to the same command.

The OPC UA namespace index is usually 3, not always: run
`factoryforge-sidecar browse opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840` once and fix `ns=` in
the mapping if yours differs.

## FF_IO

In declaration order. `PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp);
`PLC reads` is an input (a sensor, a button, a measurement). The two
directions never share a byte, so the snap7 driver never rewrites a bit your
program owns. `FF_IO` is 24 bytes. *Brief* marks the signals the task
names.

| Tag | Direction | Member | Type | Offset | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `axis.target` | PLC writes | `AxisTarget` | Real | DBD0 | target position, mm, 0..1000 | yes |
| `axis.velocity` | PLC writes | `AxisVelocity` | Real | DBD4 | move velocity, mm/s (the axis caps it at 500) | yes |
| `position_display.value` | PLC writes | `PositionDisplayValue` | DInt | DBD8 | number shown on the display (mm) | yes |
| `axis.ack` | PLC writes | `AxisAck` | Bool | DBX12.0 | acknowledge a latched error: RISING edge, and only once its cause has gone | yes |
| `axis.enable` | PLC writes | `AxisEnable` | Bool | DBX12.1 | power the drive (a level, like MC_Power.Enable) | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | `PanelGreen` | Bool | DBX12.2 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | `PanelRed` | Bool | DBX12.3 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | `TowerGreen` | Bool | DBX12.4 | tower lamp, green | yes |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | `TowerRed` | Bool | DBX12.5 | tower lamp, red | yes |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | `TowerYellow` | Bool | DBX12.6 | tower lamp, yellow | yes |
| `axis.position` | PLC reads | `AxisPosition` | Real | DBD14 | actual position, mm | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | `PanelSetpoint` | Real | DBD18 | the operator's pot, 300..950 mm (starts at 800) | yes |
| `axis.error` | PLC reads | `AxisError` | Bool | DBX22.0 | latched drive error: the axis has stopped itself and waits for an acknowledge | yes |
| `axis.fault` | PLC reads | `AxisFault` | Bool | DBX22.1 | drive fault present: TRUE = the cause of an error is still there | yes |
| `axis.inposition` | PLC reads | `AxisInposition` | Bool | DBX22.2 | stopped within 0.5 mm of the target it holds NOW -- stale on the scan you change the target | yes |
| `axis.ready` | PLC reads | `AxisReady` | Bool | DBX22.3 | powered and error-free | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | `PanelEstop` | Bool | DBX22.4 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | `PanelReset` | Bool | DBX22.5 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | `PanelStart` | Bool | DBX22.6 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | `PanelStop` | Bool | DBX22.7 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |

`int` travels as a `DInt` and `float` as a `Real`: the OPC UA driver writes
Int32 and Float, and a member of any other type is refused as a type mismatch.
Hold anything the scene must see for well over a second on OPC UA: an
S7-1500 forces a 1000 ms publishing interval on subscriptions, which is why the
driver polls by default.
